desc:
Many products need steady developer time more than one big project. Ecom Swift LLC offers monthly SaaS development hours, starting with a first block: we agree a ranked task list, work through it in your repository and update you after each work day.

## What are monthly SaaS development hours?

Monthly development means buying a block of developer time instead of a fixed feature. You supply a list of things the product needs: small features, fixes, improvements, integrations. We rank them with you, then spend the hours on them in order of value.

This page covers the first block. Think of it as a trial period: you see how we plan, communicate and ship before deciding whether to continue on a monthly plan, which we quote separately.

## Why a block of hours suits a growing product

Most SaaS products do not need a large team all the time. They need a person who knows the code, can pick up the next most useful task and finish it. Hiring that person takes months and carries fixed cost. A block of hours gives you capacity when work exists and nothing when it does not.

The risk with open-ended freelance work is drift: hours pass, the list grows and nobody can say what was completed. The structure here prevents that. The list is agreed first, changes are reviewed in the open and each day ends with a written note.

## How steady development improves your product

Products improve through many small releases, not one large launch. Each shipped fix or improvement removes a reason for a customer to leave, a support question or a manual step for your team. When that happens every week, the product feels cared for.

Ranking is where the value comes from. If you spend limited hours on the item that blocks the most customers, the effect is greater than if you spend them on whatever came to mind first. Our task list process makes that trade-off visible, so you choose it rather than discovering it later.

## What a good block of development hours includes

- A task list written before any code, with each item described in plain terms.
- A rank order based on customer impact and effort.
- Work on a branch in your own repository, never directly on your main branch.
- A short written update at the end of each work day.
- Demo notes for each change, so you can check it yourself.
- Tests for the behavior we add or change.
- Honest estimates, with a warning when a task is larger than it looked.
- A clear count of hours used and hours left.
- A recommendation on what to do in the next block.

## How we work

We begin with a list from you, even a messy one. We turn it into clear tasks, estimate them and agree what fits the hours. Work then runs in order. Your branch gets the changes, you get the update and the demo notes, and you can reorder the list at any point.

The Basic package is a first block of hours on a ranked list with daily updates. Standard adds more hours, a planning call, a tested release to staging and an end-of-week summary. Premium is a full sprint with a production release and rollback plan, daily written updates, a review call and an estimate for the following month.

If the list is longer than the hours, the remaining items stay ranked for the next block. Nothing is hidden or squeezed in carelessly.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Write tasks as outcomes, such as what a user should be able to do.
- Name one person who can make decisions quickly.
- Reply to questions within a day when you can.
- Review the demo notes as we go.
- Tell us early if priorities change.

**Avoid:**
- Handing over a very long list and expecting all of it.
- Adding large new tasks halfway through the block.
- Mixing urgent outages with planned work without saying so.
- Leaving questions unanswered, which stalls the clock.
- Skipping the review of finished changes.

## Who this is for

This suits a solo founder with a product in market and a backlog that never shrinks. It suits a small company whose only developer left. It also suits a team that wants to test a new developer partner on real work before committing to anything longer.

## What we need from you

A task list, repository access as a collaborator or developer user, and instructions for running the project locally or on staging. If your stack needs an environment file, share the structure with dummy values. We never need passwords, and we work in your own accounts so everything stays under your control.
